headline: Western Russia: One Killed in Samara Region as Ukraine Strikes Oil Refinery
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Western Russia: One Killed in Samara Region as Ukraine Strikes Oil Refinery.
- South Asia: Pakistan calls for human control over decisions on nuclear weapons use.
- Africa: Iran warns of destructive response if key facilities are attacked.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Estimates of Russians killed in Ukraine surpass all combined US war deaths since WWI.
- Military Times, 4 hours ago: Estimates of Russians killed in Ukraine surpass all combined US war deaths since WWI.
More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war in Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale war against the nation nearly five years ago.
- Military Times, 6 hours ago: All USS George Washington CSG sailors returning from deployment to be provided ashore accommodations.
Sailors from the USS George Washington carrier strike group will be able to sleep in off-ship beds when they return from their roughly six-month deployment, the Navy said.
The Caribbean - bottom line: ODPEM fiasco could scare off future donors, PNP warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 2 days ago: ODPEM fiasco could scare off future donors, PNP warns.
Local and international partners could become reluctant to donate to Jamaica in future national emergencies if confidence in the management of humanitarian aid is not urgently restored, Opposition Spokesperson on Local Government Natalie Neita Garvey has warned. This comes amid findings from a report by the auditor general that the Office of Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Management (ODPEM) misused funds donated for a Government-directed roof programme to clear third-party goods.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Argentina officially enters a technical recession.
- Buenos Aires Herald, one day ago: Argentina officially enters a technical recession.
Despite September's month-over-month growth, poor figures for July and August dragged down quarterly performance. Economists are already warning of “stagflation” La entrada Argentina officially enters a technical recession se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

25th Sicheslav Airborne Brigade has reported that Russian forces attempting to advance south of Dobropillia under cover of strong winds were stopped after FPV drone strikes and a minefield disabled their armoured vehicles.
- The Moscow Times, 6 hours ago: Russian Official Warns of Ukrainian Drone Attacks on Utility Infrastructure This Winter.
The comments mirrored warnings from Ukrainian leaders about the risk of winter attacks on energy infrastructure disrupting power and heating supplies.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russian drone attacks car in Kharkiv Oblast, killing two.
A Russian drone struck a civilian car in Kharkiv Oblast's Zolochiv hromada on 25 November, killing two people, likely a local couple, Syniehubov said.
Southern Europe - bottom line: French presidential hopeful Teddy Riner says Ukraine is ‘not our war’.
- Politico Europe, 6 hours ago: French presidential hopeful Teddy Riner says Ukraine is ‘not our war’.
The Olympic gold medalist's remarks on Russia's ongoing full-scale invasion provoked a backlash.

- Africanews, 8 hours ago: Nigeria's Borgu district grapples with aftermath of deadly communal attacks.
Residents of the Borgu district in central Nigeria were left grappling with the aftermath of deadly communal attacks on Tuesday. Assaults killed several dozens in the area during the weekend.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 18 hours ago: Sudan: Violations Against Women, Girls Escalates.
[Dabanga] Blue Nile State -- The Strategic Initiative for Women in the Horn of Africa (SIHA Network) has reported the abduction of 28 women and girls fleeing fighting in Damazin and 15 cases of conflict-related sexual violence against girls under the age of 18 in Blue Nile state. In a statement published yesterday, the organisation has warned of escalating violations against women and girls as fighting intensifies, with thousands of families fleeing their homes and facing growing humanitarian risks.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan calls for human control over decisions on nuclear weapons use.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 17 hours ago: Pakistan calls for human control over decisions on nuclear weapons use.
UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan has called for keeping decisions on the use of nuclear weapons under human control and warned that artificial intelligence (AI) systems must never be used to target nuclear command, control and communications systems. The warning was delivered by Pakistan’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, during a high-level open debate of the UN Security Council on Wednesday on conflict resolution in an era of rapid technological change.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: AJK Assembly sets conditions for resumption of dialogue with proscribed JAAC.
MUZAFFARABAD: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly on Wednesday offered to reopen negotiations with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), subject to the disbandment of armed groups, surrender of those allegedly involved in serious crimes and an unequivocal commitment to pursue demands through constitutional and democratic means. The region has witnessed violence-marred protests over the past few months, particularly in June and July, with reports of sporadic unrest in recent weeks.
- The Hindu - International, 15 hours ago: At least two Indians among 11 injured in Houthi attack in Riyadh; New Delhi condemns strike.
Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence said a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District came under what it described as a "terrorist attack" by Houthi militia
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: £190m corruption case: Imran, Bushra's counsel says transaction caused no loss to exchequer.
ISLAMABAD: In the £190 million corruption case, counsel for PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, argued that the transaction had caused no loss to the national exchequer but had instead proved financially beneficial. The couple is serving prison sentences in the £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case. On January 17, 2025, an accountability court in Islamabad sentenced Imran to 14 years in prison and Bushra to seven years in the case. Both subsequently challenged their convictions before the IHC.

He emphasized the need for coordination with the Border Security Force to strengthen border security measures. Adhikari also highlighted efforts to combat illegal activities like drug trafficking and smuggling. Additionally, he warned against violence towards women and insisted on enforcing animal protection laws.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Missing businessman's non-bailable warrant cancelled in AJL case, ED to move HC.
A special MP/MLA court in Rouse Avenue cancelled a non-bailable warrant against businessman Dinesh Pandey. The Enforcement Directorate is surprised and plans to appeal this decision in the Delhi high court. Pandey is reportedly involved in transferring Rs 10.4 crore through a shell company to Associated Journals Ltd. The court criticized the investigating officer for using a sealed cover, which is typically standard practice.

But for Hondurans, the message is less stark. “Overall, Gracias a Dios is a low-crime, functioning department,” says a State Department background report.
